title: Oak: Ancient Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Twelve mapped oaks whose exact species is unconfirmed, from a Belfast survivor down to six acorns to the 1839 land sale under Austin's Auction Oaks.
intro: Twelve oaks on this map carry only their genus, Quercus, because nobody has yet taken a leaf close enough to say which species each one is. That gap does not make them less worth the walk. Belfast's Belvoir Oak got down to six acorns one winter, all its crown could still manage, and is still standing. Ypres's Christusboom has been cut to nothing by two wars and grown back from the stump both times. Austin's Auction Oaks shaded the 1839 sale of town lots before the city existed, and the Seiders Oaks nearby saved a settler's life in a fight with mounted raiders three years later. Hainich's Betteleiche is hollow because medieval friars are said to have carved it out to keep alms dry. If you can tell a pedunculate from a sessile oak at a glance, tell us.
